comment: Real sources, checked against a running deployment by scripts/coverage.mjs.
The unit tests prove the parsing; this proves the internet still behaves.
The expectation that matters is minInWindow: coverage is how much of what a
publisher filed recently we caught, not how many articles came back. Add a
line whenever a source misbehaves in real use, with what you expect of it —
the entry becomes the thing that notices if it regresses.

sources.why: Reported five days stale. apnews.com 403s every path, so this checks the aggregator route is still fresh — a wire whose newest story is hours old is the failure.
Reported missing stories: this is where the WSJ files everything.
A section must stay a section, not widen to the whole paper.
No feed, two posts: the scraper's minimum used to refuse it.
An ordinary declared RSS feed — the common case.
An independent blog syndicating full text in Atom.
A government listing page with no feed of its own.
A news sitemap ten times deeper than the feed: the case the union design exists for.
Declares no RSS at all — if this returns nothing, the sitemap route has broken.
The reverse case: its feed carries more than its sitemap, so the merge must keep both.
A section that must stay one: the site sitemap covers the whole newsroom.
